video_title: Nikola Jokic Future in Denver, Jaylen Brown Trade Market & more | Third Apron Podcast

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Nikola Jokic's future and the possibility of a trade
quotes.excerpt: We have to at least have the conversation about his future because he can become a free agent
quotes.quote: For years and years, what we heard from Bucks fans was it's so unfair that you do this with Giannis and you fake trade him all the time and you say he has to leave Milwaukee. Why don't you ever do it with Jokic? And I think the reason we didn't do it with Jokic, it was warranted, because he didn't do the passive-aggressive quotes in the media. It didn't feel like he was constantly pressuring the team. His messaging was always really consistent. It was always, I want to retire with the Nuggets, I want to spend my whole career here, I love it here, I am happy here. He is now going into a contract year without extending, or at least for now, we have heard from Mark Stein and Jake Fischer that he may not extend this offseason, which means he can become a free agent in 2027. For anyone else, we would be saying it is time for a trade. I am not going to sit here and say it is time for a Nikola Jokic trade, but we have to at least have the conversation about his future because he can become a free agent next offseason and therefore leave for nothing.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Financial implications of Nikola Jokic not signing an extension
quotes.excerpt: If he doesn't extend, then he could hit free agency next year and he can do a five-year contract
quotes.quote: The biggest one is there is another financial component to this where if he doesn't extend, then he could hit free agency next year and he can do a five-year contract. So get a fifth year instead of securing four more now. Really, he would be securing three now because he has got that player option and the more lucrative option would be to pick up that player option, just based on where the salary cap is projected to rise, and then add three years on top of that. So he is really securing three years now and then if he does the opt-out next year as a free agent, he would be like securing four guaranteed more years.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Nuggets' salary cap situation and tax implications
quotes.excerpt: It looks like the Nuggets are going to cut salary so they can resign Peyton Watson
quotes.quote: Most stars try to extend as early as possible because most stars are worried about getting hurt and losing their value. That is not really a concern with Jokic, just given the way that he plays. He got hurt last year, but he barely ever gets hurt and he doesn't play a style where like, if he tore his Achilles, would his value really change that much? No, he would still get a max. So there is no real reason for him to extend as early as possible in the way that there is for other guys, especially in the financially conscious apron era. I don't think this is as simple as, yeah, we will do it later, no problem. I think at the very least, this is him exerting pressure on the Nuggets because what have we been saying all offseason? It looks like the Nuggets are going to cut salary so they can resign Peyton Watson without incurring a like nine-figure tax bill. And where they are at right now, before waiving Jonas Valanciunas, which I assume they are going to do, they are like 3 million below the second apron.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Nuggets' financial constraints and roster building
quotes.excerpt: They just dumped Michael Porter Jr. last year. I understand why they did it
quotes.quote: If it ever got to a point where he no longer wants to be with the Nuggets, he has, like he can look into the quote-unquote cheapness, whatever it is, holding back on spending, because the Nuggets are in a very sensitive situation spending-wise and this is even independent from whatever ownership is willing to spend. These numbers are pretty untenable because right now they are already still in the repeater tax, looking at like, without, they still need to fill out four roster spots where if they just gave minimum salaries, they are going to have, I don't know, an 80 million dollar tax penalty, right now it is at 44 and a half. They just dumped Michael Porter Jr. last year. I understand why they did it, but if I am Jokic, you know, I, I don't really necessarily would take the financial implications all that positively and now it seems like they are going to do something like that again.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Players' perspective on team spending and luxury tax
quotes.excerpt: Players don't care about your luxury tax bill. The famous one that I always go back to is Miami
quotes.quote: Players don't care about your luxury tax bill. The famous one that I always go back to is Miami coming off of a second consecutive championship using the amnesty provision on Mike Miller because they thought that he wasn't going to be healthy enough moving forward so they just wanted to save the luxury tax bill and then Mike Miller goes on and plays 82 games for the Grizzlies that year. LeBron leaves a year after and LeBron has not been subtle about exerting his power as a franchise player to force his teams to spend since then. Players don't care about your margins. Players don't care if you're profitable as a franchise. They care are you doing everything in your power to put a winning roster around them? And I'm sorry, if you're dumping Cam Johnson to lower your tax bill, that is a slap in Nikola Jokic's face.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Nuggets' championship outlook and Jokic's injury impact
quotes.excerpt: I am a real believer that Jokic's wrist injury was worse than people thought
quotes.quote: I don't think they are as bad as they looked in the Minnesota series. I am a real believer that Jokic's wrist injury was worse than people thought and that is why he wasn't making threes and a lot of stuff trickles downstream from his inability to make threes. Peyton Watson didn't play in that series, Aaron Gordon was hurt. I don't think they are that bad, but let's be realistic. Their odds of beating the Thunder or the Spurs, let alone both and somebody in the East, is relatively low moving forward, right? If he wants to win another championship and he has not said the things that Giannis said where winning another championship is more important than retiring with his original team. But if that is something that he cares about, it is probably not going to happen in Denver.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Hypothetical strategy to suppress Peyton Watson's market
quotes.excerpt: Say you were the Nuggets and you wanted to suppress Peyton Watson's market in restricted free agency
quotes.quote: Can I pitch you something that I just thought of, in theory? I don't think this is what is happening, it is just an interesting thought. Say you were the Nuggets and you wanted to suppress Peyton Watson's market in restricted free agency. One way you could do that was put out into the world that Nikola Jokic might be a free agent in 2027, so you better not spend your cap space in 2026. I wonder if there is any, I don't think that is the case to be clear, but it would be kind of a genius thing by the Nuggets if they thought the Lakers were going to throw a bunch of money at Peyton Watson to be like, ooh, I don't know if you should do that, because you don't want to spend cap space that you could use on Jokic next year.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Prediction on Nikola Jokic's contract extension
quotes.excerpt: I think he is eventually going to extend and I think the Nuggets are going to blink
quotes.quote: I think he is eventually going to extend and I think the Nuggets are going to blink on the giant tax bill because something to keep in mind is that Cam Johnson is expiring. So you could just have the giant tax bill this year and then save a bunch of money next year. They wouldn't be cheap after that, don't get me wrong, but like the thought of having the 100 million dollar plus payroll would be a one-year thing. And I just think if you're in a position as Denver's ownership, where the options are pay a 100 million dollar tax bill but you know that is going to keep Jokic, or don't roll the dice, I think they would blink before he would.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Teams that could potentially trade for Nikola Jokic
quotes.excerpt: There are only three viable teams. One of them in free agency, two through a rental trade
quotes.quote: I think there are only three viable teams. One of them in free agency, two through a rental trade. If you are going to get traded, you can use the threat of the Lakers to lower the cost for anybody else where it is basically like, somebody is paying a rental price and you can kind of wink-wink to them and say, maybe I will extend, I will extend with you only, blah, blah, blah. Because we just saw that Miami had to overpay to secure Giannis and now the Heat are in a really dangerous situation where they might not have enough left over to build a contender around him.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Nikola Jokic to LeBron James and Kevin Durant
quotes.excerpt: I look at Nikola Jokic as a caliber of player that is just very, very, very rarely
quotes.quote: I look at Nikola Jokic as a caliber of player that is just very, very, very rarely in this situation. And the only comparable players I can think of are LeBron James and Kevin Durant. Between the two of them, in the 2010s, they became free agents five times. At no point, none of those free agencies were precipitated with a trade. The Cavs could have traded LeBron in 2010 or in 2018, they did not. The Heat could have traded LeBron in 2014, they did not. The Thunder could have traded Kevin Durant in 2016, they did not. The Warriors could have traded Kevin Durant in 2019, they did not. I think there is a class of player who is so singularly valuable that there is nothing you could trade them for that would be worthwhile.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Championship equity provided by having Nikola Jokic
quotes.excerpt: I think merely having Nikola Jokic on your roster as the Nuggets creates an amount of championship equity
quotes.quote: I think merely having Nikola Jokic on your roster as the Nuggets creates an amount of championship equity that 10 first-round picks would not replicate. I would rather have a 20% chance to resign him in free agency than five first-round picks. So I really think unless Nikola Jokic goes to the Nuggets and says directly, I am not resigning, it is time to trade me, they will not trade him. I think this is the rare situation where they would play this out into free agency and force him to say I am leaving.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Why a trade for Nikola Jokic is unlikely
quotes.excerpt: I think with Giannis there was some actual reason to keep signing the extensions for like health
quotes.quote: The reason I disagree with you is I think with Giannis there was some actual reason to keep signing the extensions for like health security reasons, secure the money. That isn't the case with Jokic. He is already only one year away from free agency and he or the people in his camp have to know that if he ever does want to change teams, if he is on a long-term contract, the Nuggets are going to be able to extract like every asset that that team has. So if he wants to move and he actually wants to win where he goes, I actually think his best move is to like stay on this expiring contract where if you are going to go to the Lakers, you can just sign into their cap space. They will have money.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Internal discussions regarding a potential Jaylen Brown trade
quotes.excerpt: There was reporting from Stein and Fischer... that the Nuggets have had internal conversations about whether or not
quotes.quote: We should tie this in because there was reporting from Stein and Fischer, I never know which of them is reporting in the newsletter, that the Nuggets have had internal conversations about whether or not they can pursue Jaylen Brown. And we should talk about that because if the Nuggets are scared, that is the sort of thing that compels you to do something as drastic as trading for Jaylen Brown. The problem here is, trading for Jaylen Brown is an enormously complicated undertaking for where the Nuggets are. Jaylen Brown makes more money than Jamal Murray.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Financial challenges of a potential Jaylen Brown trade
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Brown makes more money than Jamal Murray. And let's assume for the sake of this conversation
quotes.quote: Jaylen Brown makes more money than Jamal Murray. And let's assume for the sake of this conversation that the Celtics are willing to trade Jaylen Brown for Jamal Murray as the base of a trade. I don't know that they are, but let's just move forward with that assumption. Jaylen Brown makes more money than Jamal Murray, which means you can't trade them one-for-one because that would trigger a first apron hard cap. The Nuggets are so far beyond the first apron that they can't deal with that. Therefore, Denver has to aggregate. And when you aggregate, you trigger a second apron hard cap. The Nuggets for the time being can't trigger a second apron hard cap.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's trade market and Celtics' potential interest
quotes.excerpt: Now that he didn't get traded for Giannis, this is the first time that we're starting to hear
quotes.quote: Now that he didn't get traded for Giannis, this is the first time that we're starting to hear now after that fell apart that the Celtics are listening to offers on him and I'm not even totally convinced that they do trade him. I'm sure they were, they repair the relationship once before when he was available for KD, I'm sure they could do it again. But let's, let's talk about this. Let's see like, what if you're Boston, what are you looking for in exchange for Jaylen Brown?

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: What the Celtics would want in a Jaylen Brown trade
quotes.excerpt: The short answer is liquidity, right? Like I don't know if there's a single team that has everything
quotes.quote: The short answer is liquidity, right? Like I don't know if there's a single team that has everything that you want. But we've heard that they want four first-round picks for him and it's like, well, that makes sense. You can go turn around and spend four first-round picks on the stuff that you do want. So my idea here is, get younger, get cheaper, break him up into several players. So should we talk about analytics gate or should we talk about the Portland stuff? What sounds more interesting to you?

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's trade value and analytics
quotes.excerpt: Bobby Marks comes out today and basically says, oh, his value is much lower around the league
quotes.quote: Bobby Marks comes out today and basically says, oh, his value is much lower around the league than people think. There was one analytics person that said he is the seventh best player on the Celtics and Jaylen Brown has come out on Twitter and is not happy about that. I do think it is worth talking about the point here though. Jaylen Brown is not the seventh best player on the Celtics, that is like very clearly wrong. He is probably like around the 20th best player in the NBA. Does that sound reasonable to you? He was a second team All-NBA player last year. I think we are both in the camp that he was not, he is not quite that that good. He is like a top 20 player. He is very good, but he is not. The MVP stuff was ridiculous and if you look at his shooting over the course of the season, it was really just outlier mid-range shooting that was, you know, keeping him in the MVP conversation early and an overperformance from the team that did later on.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Miami Heat trade options for Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.excerpt: Can they match money as it is or would they have to give up Jimmy Butler?

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Quinn
text_blocks.text: Can they match money as it is or would they have to give up Jimmy Butler?

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: I don't think they have to. They could do Draymond. They could figure it out.

quotes.speaker: Sam Quinn
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. remains a prominent trade candidate for Denver
quotes.excerpt: He becomes one of the more prominent guys left that they have been linked to
quotes.quote: My point there is he becomes one of the more prominent guys left that they have been linked to at some point in the past. If they are getting Hachimura, I am looking like, okay, or maybe they revisit with Detroit or whatever. But that is where I look and I say it feels like Porter is probably moving.
